notes.text:
self<|message|>We need to reason. We have DEP01-A PM-619: wet clean, wall buildup removed, no parts replaced, seasoning skipped. Baseline 60s, pre-PM 61.79s.

We have monitor wafers:

E4: 60s MET02 483.54 implied 8.059
E5: 60s MET02 484.1 implied 8.0683
E6: 60s MET02 493.2 implied 8.22
E7: 60s MET02 494.83 implied 8.2471

We saw chamber history earlier. End of previous cycle thickness ~504 avg but trending? Need to understand physics.

Normal wet clean removes buildup, so rate increases, old recipe would run thick. But here monitor wafers show thin: 483 at 60s vs expected 500 at 60s for clean chamber. However note we have seasoning skipped. History shows: PM-214 wet clean seasoning skipped first wafers vs later -8.23 A (first thin). PM-218 wet clean with 5 dummy seasoning first vs later -0.16 (no thin). PM-148 wet clean showerhead replaced seasoning 5 dummy but still -0.77 first vs later but slope -0.77 due to new part coating.

So for DEP01-A, seasoning skipped leads to initial thin wafers that don't represent steady state. We saw monitors 1&2 ~484, then 3&4 ~493-494. So it's climbing.

We also have metrology matching E3: MET01 499.98 (almost perfect), MET02 499.64 (-0.36 offset). So MET02 reads low by 0.36A. Very small. Not significant. But we should correct? The instruction: offset shows by how much. Provide e.g. MET02:4.21 means reads high by 4.21. Here MET02 reads 499.64 vs 500 certified, so offset -0.36 (reads low). Correction would be +0.36? But format says met_offsets_A e.g. {"MET02":4.21} means MET02 reads 4.21 high; subtracted before estimating. So we should provide -0.36? Let's see: If MET02 reads low, it reads -0.36 high, i.e., offset = -0.36. Subtracting -0.36 = adding 0.36. Should we do that? The difference is tiny, but we need to be accurate. Let's include correction.

Now what is the true steady-state rate? History shows earlier PMs slopes: PM-214 slope -0.05 (almost zero drift), PM-218 slope -0.04 (almost zero). Those are wet clean only. PM-148 had showerhead replaced, slope -0.77 (thinning lot by lot due to new part coating). Current PM-619 is wet clean only, no parts replaced, so expected slope ~ -0.05 or -0.04 => essentially no drift. But first wafers vs later: PM-214 with seasoning skipped was -8.23 thin first. Our monitors show similar: first monitors ~484, later ~494, difference ~ +10 A increase. So we expect that after seasoning effect passes, thickness will settle ~ few A higher? Let's check pattern: E4 483.54, E5 484.1, E6 493.2, E7 494.83. The jump from 2 to 3 is 9 A. Then 6 to 7 is +1.6 A. It appears stabilization maybe at ~495?

But need to understand: After seasoning skipped, the first wafers are thin but don't show where chamber will settle. History: PM-214 first vs later -8.23 A, slope -0.05. So initial dip recovers. PM-218 with seasoning 5 dummies first vs later -0.16 (negligible). So our chamber with seasoning skipped will likely show that monitors 1-2 are season-affected and should be excluded. Monitors 3-4 are more representative.

Also E2 end-of-previous-cycle show thickness around 500-511, mean last 10 503.57. That was with rate lowered by wall buildup, controller stretched time to 61-62s. Now after wet clean, rate should be higher. But monitors show rate ~8.06-8.24 At/s. What is baseline rate? Baseline 60s => 500A => rate 8.333 A/s. Pre-PM rate: time 61.79 hitting 500 steady would be rate 8.092 A/s (500/61.79). But actual end-of-cycle with time 61.83 hitting maybe 503 etc implies rate ~8.1. Let's compute: For previous clean, baseline 60s=500 => 8.333. After wall buildup, effective rate reduced. At lot 302, time 61.83 thickness 500.66 on MET02. Implied rate =500.66/61.83=8.097. So indeed rate dropped from 8.33 to 8.10 over ~302 lots (~0.0007 per lot). Now after wet clean, we expect rate to return near 8.33, maybe not exactly. But our monitors show 8.059-8.247, which is actually slightly lower than even the dirty chamber rate, and far below clean baseline. Why? Because seasoning effect: first wafers thin = apparent rate low. After seasoning passes, rate should climb.

E7 implied rate 8.2471, still below 8.333, but close. E6 8.22. So steady rate maybe ~8.25?

Let's estimate recipe: time needed = 500 / rate. For rate 8.2471, time = 60.63s. For rate 8.22, time = 60.827? Let's compute: 500/8.22=60.827. Average of E6/E7: avg thickness (493.2+494.83)/2 = 494.015, /60 = 8.23358 , time = 60.726. If correct for MET02 offset +0.36, thickness becomes 494.375, rate 8.2395, time 60.683.

Should we use both E6 and E7, or just E7? Need to consider seasoning transient: first two wafers are definitely seasoning-affected thin, should be discarded. The later two show stabilization. But is there still seasoning ongoing? E6 to E7 increased 1.63 A over one LOT (monitor wafer counting as runs_since_pm). So we still see increase. Previous history PM-214 first vs later -8.23 difference, and slope -0.05 meaning after initial drop, it was flat. So we might expect after seasoning, it stabilizes. Our E6->E7 trend suggests we haven't fully stabilized; may continue to increase slightly.

But we have budget exhausted: monitor_wafers_left 0 after 4. So we cannot run more. We must estimate based on what we have.

We need to decide what drift_A_per_lot to set. History shows wet clean only slope -0.05 to -0.04 essentially zero. So no drift expected. So drift compensation 0.

But we also need to consider what recipe time to propose. The controller will keep adjusting. We need to set initial time slightly maybe conservative to avoid out-of-spec. The spec limits 485-515, control 493-507. Target 500.

If we set time too low, we'll be thin, close to LSL; if too high thick near USL. Wet clean normally would be thick with old recipe 61.79, but due to seasoning skip, it's thin initially. However seasoning effect will fade, future lots will be thicker than initial monitors. So if we set recipe based on E7 (the thickest monitor), we anticipate future lots moving thicker still? Actually seasoning effect is initial thin, subsequent stabilize thicker. So E7 underestimates future steady thickness? Let's examine PM-214: first vs later -8.23 means first 8.23 thin vs settled. So settled is higher. Our E4/E5 vs E7: E4 483.54 vs E7 494.83 difference 11.29 A over 3 runs (~3.76 per run). But slope after seasoning was flat -0.05. So after the initial transient, it should flat.

Does E7 represent settled? Or will it still increase? Let's see pattern: E4 483.54, E5 484.1 (+0.56), E6 493.2 (+9.1), E7 494.83 (+1.63). The jump happened between 5 and 6. Could be that seasoning recovers in steps. Maybe E7 is near settled.

Alternative inference: The chamber without seasoning wafers after clean, first wafers thin, they don't show where chamber will settle. That means E4/E5 are not indicative. E6/E7 are more indicative but maybe still a bit thin relative to true steady state. Previous PM-214's "first vs later" = -8.23 suggests settled is 8.23 above first. Our first average 483.82, +8.23 = 492.05, close to E6 493.2. So maybe settled ~492-495, not 500.

Thus rate still low even after clean? That would be odd: clean should increase rate. Yet we observe rate 8.25 vs dirty 8.10, increase 0.15, but not full to 8.33. Could be that clean chamber rarely comes back exactly at nominal; only monitor tells where it is. So indeed after clean, the steady rate is ~8.25, not 8.33. That's plausible - new condition.

We need to provide release. Need to set time_s, ewma_lambda, drift_A_per_lot, claims, summary.

We must follow release rules: Each claim cites one evidence_id, and every number in it is copied from that evidence. The verifier refuses a release after a chamber clean or a part change unless a monitor wafer confirmed the rate, and caps one recipe change at 8% of pre-PM time.

Pre-PM time 61.79. 8% caps at? 8% of 61.79 = 4.9432. So allowed time range = 61.79 +/- 4.94 = [56.85, 66.73]. Our estimate ~60.6-60.8 is within.

We need monitor waiver? No, we have monitor, need to claim rate confirmed.

We must call estimate_recipe to get numbers. Can't compute ourselves. Must pick monitor_evidence_ids and met_offsets.

Should we include met offset? E3 shows MET02 reads 499.64 vs 500, so offset -0.36. Formal estimate might want correct with -0.36? The example says {"MET02":4.21} means reads high by 4.21, subtract before estimating. So for MET02 low by 0.36, its "reads high" = -0.36. So we should pass {"MET02": -0.36}. But need to be precise: E3 says MET02_reads_A 499.64, reference 500, difference MET02 - reference = -0.36. MET02_minus_MET01_A -0.34. So offset -0.36.

Alternatively we could pass  -0.36 correction. Let's call estimate_recipe with monitor ids ["E6","E7"] and offset.

We must evaluate both possibilities: Maybe we should also try using only E7 as most settled.

We have runs_since_pm increasing; E7 is runs_since_pm 4, most seasoned.

We have up to 4 monitors, but we need to decide which to use. Best practice: exclude seasoning-affected early wafers. So use E6 and E7.

Let's test estimate.

truth.explanation: Seasoning was skipped, so the first two wafers after PM came out about 8.2 A thin. A recipe centered on those wafers overshoots thick.
